title: Session-store ghost entries and mixed-precision memory cascade causing multi-environment GPU OOMs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported rapid GPU OOM cascades that started after a low-latency burst workload (short chat sessions with long prefix tokens). Investigation shows a sequence: mixed-precision kernels triggered spill-to-host for intermittent tensors, which increased fragmentation of the tensor arena. Concurrently, a regression in the session-store eviction path left transient 'ghost' entries (zero-sized tombstones) in the session index. Over time these ghost entries prevented compaction and produced an index skew that made KV lookups allocate small metadata slabs repeatedly. The combination of arena fragmentation, repeated tiny allocations, and mixed-precision spill increased device memory pressure and led to node-wide OOMs. Incidents occurred in Hosted (autoscale bursts), Dedicated (predictable commit pools under heavy multi-tenant noise), and Private (on-prem with slightly older CUDA drivers).
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy runtime-1.22 on a test pool with mixed-precision enabled and tensor-arena sizing set to default
2) Start 400 short chat sessions that include a common long prefix (1000 tokens) to exercise KV prefix caching and KV-metadata hot paths

3) Interleave some requests with responses that force fp16->fp32 upcasts (simulated by our test harness), and simultaneously run an eviction stressor against session-store (rapid create/delete of session handles),
4) Observe device memory usage growth in tensor arena, spikes in host spill metrics, and increase in 'session-ghosts' metric exposed by session-store telemetry
5) Eventually a node reports GPU OOM and session failures propagate to 5xx responses for downstream customers
impact_summary: Customer-facing 5xx errors, elevated latency during bursts, and at least two P0 escalations from enterprise tenants on Dedicated capacity. Host nodes needed manual recycle in some Hosted regions and a coordinated kernel driver upgrade in one Private deployment to stabilize behaviour.
mitigation_summary: Immediate mitigations instituted: (a) roll out a temporary throttler on bursty conversation endpoints to limit concurrent short sessions, (b) enable conservative arena compaction on affected pools, (c) deploy a hotpatch that forces session-store tombstone reclamation every 30s, and (d) temporarily disable the FP32 upcast fallback on selected model variants. These reduced OOM frequency while the full fix was developed.
root_cause_summary: Root cause is the intersection of three faults: (1) a recent change in the allocator that delayed slab compaction under fragmentation patterns produced by mixed-precision spills, (2) a regression in session-store eviction which left zero-sized ghost entries preventing normal index compaction, and (3) a scheduling pattern that amplified small allocation churn under high concurrency. Individually these were tolerable; together they produced a cascading memory pressure leading to OOMs.
decisions: 1) Patch allocator to trigger eager compaction when host-spill events exceed threshold
2) Revert the session-store eviction regression and add an invariant check that fails early if ghost entries exceed 1% of index size
3) Add a mixed-precision kernel telemetry flag to enable rapid identification of spill-heavy workloads
4) Backport minimal fixes to runtime-1.21 for customers on older pinned releases
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (hotfix, 2026-03-11): push session-store tombstone reclamation hotpatch to Hosted pools and notify Dedicated infra teams; monitor for recurrence
Phase 1 (patch, 2026-03-13): release allocator compaction change + session-store regression revert to runtime-1.22-canary and run multi-tenant soak for 48h
Phase 2 (gradual rollout, 2026-03-14 to 2026-03-18): promote to 25%/50%/100% across regions with automatic rollback on OOM signal
Phase 3 (backports, by 2026-03-20): backport hotfixes to runtime-1.21 for Dedicated/Private customers that request pinning
follow_up_tasks: Create an allocator regression test that simulates mixed-precision spill and high churn to catch future compaction regressions
Add a session-store index health dashboard and an alert when ghost entries trend up for more than 5 minutes
Perform a postmortem and include operator runbook additions for burst throttling and kernel-driver guidance for Private customers
Schedule a runtime hygiene week to audit other eviction paths and light-weight allocator tweaks
